svg.title: Booster landing: the hoverslam
svg.desc: Animated altitude-versus-time plot of a reusable booster's landing burn (hoverslam), next to a booster icon that descends on the same altitude scale. Numbers from site/data/booster.json and booster-physics.js: mass 26,700 kg (22,200 kg dry + 4,500 kg propellant, the 'final approach' scenario), one Merlin 1D at 80% of 845 kN sea-level thrust = 676 kN, falling at terminal velocity ≈ 200 m/s (scripts/test_booster.mjs: ≈200 m/s at sea level) from 3,000 m. a_net = T/m − g = 15.51 m/s²; burn height h = v²/(2·a_net) = 1,289 m; burn time v/a_net = 12.9 s; coast 8.6 s; touchdown at 21.4 s. Minimum throttle 482 kN vs weight 262 kN gives T/W = 1.84 > 1, so it cannot hover. Ghosts: lit at 2,000 m it stops 711 m up and then climbs even at minimum throttle; lit at 1,000 m it hits the deck at 95 m/s. Idealised: constant mass and no drag during the burn (both would help: the stage gets lighter and air still brakes it).
svg.text: It can't hover, so it has to time the burn
lit at 1,289 m: 0 m/s at 0 m
lit at 2,000 m: stops 711 m up, then climbs
lit at 1,000 m: hits the deck at 95 m/s
Falcon 9-class stage, 26.7 t, falling at 200 m/s; one engine at 80 % · 2× speed
